_comment: Order & Conquest — all tunable numbers live here as DATA, not in code.
OrderAndConquest.Engine loads this once at startup and binds it to RulesConfig.
Values marked SOURCED are supported by docs/12-references.md.
Values marked ASSUMPTION are design decisions recorded in docs/00-decisions-and-assumptions.md.
Changing a value here must never require an engine rebuild.
* seaRoutes.min/max/default REMOVED — routes are a fixed list per map (D-37),
authored in shared/maps/world_classic.json, not generated per match.
* airForce.enabled and navalForce.enabled are now FALSE (D-54). The first
version is exactly classic RISK; the extensions are switched on per match.
* ai.difficulty REMOVED (D-21 retired). The lobby offers bot NAMES, not
difficulty levels. MarsBot's W_p is still the tuning dial.
* match.turnTimerSeconds REMOVED (D-65). Nothing in this game expires.
* network section ADDED (D-43, D-60, D-61, D-66).
THE MOST IMPORTANT THING IN THIS FILE: the engine must NOT read combat.diceSides
or combat.attackRange live from here once a match exists. Both are copied into
the match_rules TABLE at creation and read from there (D-52). See _note_frozen.

setup._note: startingArmies is SOURCED. 2-player uses a third Neutral seat, so the 3-player row (35) applies (D-07, confirmed D-62). The Neutral seat appears in 2-player matches ONLY. territoryAllocation: 'claim' | 'random'.

draft._note: SOURCED: armies = max(3, floor(territories / 3)) + continent bonuses + card trade value.

combat._note: SOURCED. defenderWinsTies is the single highest-risk flag in this file; TC-CMB-02…06 assert the exact odds fractions against it.
combat._note_diceSides: D-29, post-lock supervisory addition. Default 6 reproduces classic RISK exactly. Faces are drawn as NextInt(1, diceSides+1); the NUMBER of draws is unchanged, so rng_position semantics are identical at every value. defenderWinsTies is independent of this key (strict > on two drawn values).
combat._note_attackRange: D-30, post-lock supervisory addition. Default 1 IS adjacency, so the default legal set equals the neighbour list. Above 1, a land attack is a BFS to depth attackRange over LAND EDGES ONLY — the same range function the Air Force uses (D-11). attackRangeMax 10 is the measured diameter of the classic land graph; larger values are meaningless. Raising this can never make a sea route traversable (C-08).
combat._note_frozen: BOTH diceSides and attackRange are copied into the match_rules TABLE at match creation and read from there, never live from this file (D-29/D-30 consequence 1, storage changed by D-52). Editing them here must not affect a match in progress: diceSides would change drawn faces while consuming identical rng_position values, and attackRange would invalidate a logged action's legality. TC-PER-07 is the guard. NOTE that TC-DET-01..04 CANNOT detect a live diceSides read: the draw COUNT is unchanged, so rng_position tracks the log perfectly while every face differs. TC-ARC-03 covers the no-hidden-state side of the same property.
combat._note_ui: D-39: NEITHER value is shown in the user interface. There is no dice-face stepper and no attack-range stepper on any screen. They are set per match at creation; docs/16-task-day-change-guide.md is the procedure for changing one if the committee asks on task day.

_note: tradeValues: 4, 6, 8, 20 and 25 are SOURCED; 10, 12, 15 are inferred and stay as data for exactly that reason.
setSize stays 3 (3-alike, 3-different, or 2 + Wild). Locked: five-card sets are NOT introduced.
symbols has 6 entries but the trade structure is unchanged from classic RISK.

distinctSetRule (D-27): 'any_distinct' = any three distinct non-Wild symbols. Alternative 'classic_triple' = specifically Infantry + Cavalry + Artillery. With five non-Wild symbols these differ; with classic RISK's three they do not.

wildSubstitution (D-28): 'joker' = a Wild stands for any symbol, so any two cards plus a Wild form a set (the official classic-RISK rule). Alternative 'pair_only' = a Wild only completes a pair, so {Infantry, Cavalry, Wild} and {X, Wild, Wild} are NOT sets.

D-27 and D-28 both need a reviewer's confirmation before Phase 4: they change how often a forced trade (FR-35) is satisfiable, and therefore every card-family test oracle. TC-CRD-06 asserts whichever branch is configured here.

capability._note: ASSUMPTION CAP-2: a seat holds capability X iff it owns >=1 territory whose profile contains X, or holds >=1 card whose profile contains X. Infantry/Cavalry/Artillery unlock nothing — they are card symbols only, exactly as in classic RISK.

_note: D-54: enabled is now FALSE by default. The first version is exactly classic RISK (D-36).
Switch it on per match via match_rules.air_force_enabled, not by editing this file.
LOCKED: maxRange 5, measured by land adjacency only. Sea routes are excluded from range.
ASSUMPTION AIR-1: attacksPerTurn = 1 is the simplest limiter that stops Air Force strictly dominating normal attack. One integer, tunable.

On the classic board, range 5 reaches 77.2% of ordered territory pairs — 1330 of 1722, graph diameter 10. RE-MEASURED 13 Oct 2026 by tools/generate_map_seed.py --stats; see docs/07-game-design.md 7.8.
D-54: enabled is now FALSE by default. Switch it on per match via match_rules.naval_force_enabled.
WARNING: enabling Naval Force while the sea_routes table is EMPTY gives the capability nothing to do. Add at least one route first (see seaRoutes below).
LOCKED: operates over sea routes only; landlocked territories are never automatically naval.
ASSUMPTION NAV-1: unitsRequiredPerRoute = 0. A sea route behaves exactly like a land edge for a seat that holds Naval capability. This is the simplest consistent rule and adds no new unit type.
D-37 REPLACED D-13 (SEA-1). Sea routes are a FIXED LIST PER MAP, authored by the team in
shared/maps/world_classic.json -> seaRoutes, and seeded into the sea_routes table. The team
wants MORE routes than classic RISK has; the schema supports any number.
REMOVED by D-37: min, max, default, maxGenerationAttempts. The host no longer chooses a
count at match setup, the system no longer picks endpoints, and screen S-05 is retired.
source: 'map' means the routes come from the map tables. There is no other value; the key
exists so that a future generator would have somewhere to declare itself.
The three validity rules SURVIVE D-37 unchanged and are now enforced in two places:
tools/generate_map_seed.py refuses to emit an invalid route, and tools/verify_db.sql
queries V1 and V2 fail if one reached the database another way.
D-59: appendices/C-map-specification.md holds a PROPOSED list of 8 routes for the team to
accept or edit. Until they do, the list is empty — which is harmless, because Naval Force
is off by default.

fortify._note: mode: 'single_pair' | 'one_step_all' | 'connected_path'. SOURCED that published rules disagree; single_pair is the default and the variant is data so a trained RL checkpoint can assert which one it learned.

match._note: roundCap 100 is SOURCED (MARS). aiMinimumThinkTimeMs is applied at the API layer, not in the agent, so RL training runs at full speed (D-22). turnTimerSeconds was REMOVED by D-65: nothing in this game expires, so the field is gone rather than present-and-zero.

_note: ADDED October 2026. The demo runs on a phone hotspot with NO INTERNET (D-34).
pollIntervalMs (D-43, D-66): clients call GET /matches/{id}/state?since={version} about once
a second. The server answers 304 Not Modified when `since` equals the current version, and
409 Conflict with the current state when a SUBMITTED action carries a stale version. There is
no WebSocket and no SignalR hub; that transport is deferred (D-47).
scheme is 'http', not 'https': there is no certificate authority on a hotspot. This is why
all three Android apps must enable cleartext traffic (D-49) — see
docs/14-implementation-safety-checklist.md. It is a demo-network decision, not a security
position; NFR-09 (hashed passwords) is unaffected.
tokenLifetimeHours 12 (D-61): long enough that a token issued at the start of task day cannot
expire during it. No refresh token, no sessions table.
roomCodeAlphabet (D-60) is 32 characters and deliberately excludes I, O, 0 and 1, which are
the pairs people mishear and mistype when a code is read aloud across a room. 4 characters
from 32 is 1,048,576 combinations.
MARS coefficients are SOURCED. W_p is the difficulty dial.
ai.difficulty was REMOVED by D-56 (which retires D-21). Difficulty is no longer a
user-facing concept: the lobby offers four BOT NAMES and the host picks one per AI seat.
The old mapping was Easy=PassiveBot, Normal=MarsBot W_p 0.85, Hard=MarsBot W_p 0.7375,
Brutal=OnnxPolicyAgent. If the team wants an easier Mars, set W_p to 0.85 here — the dial
survived, only the wrapper is gone.
TIERS (D-56): PassiveBot and MarsBot are [P1] and must work for the demo. ChaoticBot and
AggressiveBot are [P2]. OnnxPolicyAgent is [P3] and is deliberately absent from both this
list and the seats.ai_agent CHECK constraint — adding it is a one-line migration if RL
ever ships (O-03).
All four names appear in the lobby mock-ups, because drawing four rows costs nothing and
redrawing the screen later costs an afternoon.

rl.shipGate: must beat MarsBot head-to-head over >=1000 seeded matches
rl._note: RL is DEFERRED (D-47) — kept in the documents, not built in this prototype. The game is complete and shippable on heuristic AI alone. Nothing in the engine, API, database or clients depends on rl.*, and seats.ai_agent deliberately does not list an ONNX agent. O-03 stays open; the honest answer for this version is 'not attempted'.
